studies.name: Saran, White & Kuper — Evidence and gap map of studies assessing the effectiveness of interventions for people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries
studies.draft_uses: 2020 publication (Campbell Systematic Reviews, 16(1), e1070); cited as [2]. Draft notes a published correction it could not hold, yet the body text draws on this source for claims about income-country distribution and evidence gaps.
studies.latest_known: A corrigendum (e1104) was published 12 July 2020, correcting the income-country distribution sentence from 'Over half (n=50) the impact evaluations come from lower-middle income countries' to 'Almost half (n=50)…'. The draft's paraphrase ('most studies come from upper-middle-income countries') does not reproduce the corrected or uncorrected sentence verbatim, but the underlying figure it implies (upper-middle-income as the dominant group) is consistent with the corrected text. No full update or new version of this EGM was found.
studies.what_changed: The corrigendum changes 'Over half (n=50) the impact evaluations come from lower-middle income countries' to 'Almost half (n=50)…, closely followed by upper-middle income countries (n=48)'. The draft's paraphrase attributes dominance to upper-middle-income countries, which aligns with the corrected text but not the original. Because the draft states it could not hold the correction yet draws on this source anyway, the figures used cannot be positively confirmed against the corrected version.

studies.latest_known: A corrigendum exists (PubMed PMID 36913230, corrects DOI 10.1002/cl2.1287, published 2023). The content of the corrigendum could not be established from search results. No full update or new version found.
studies.what_changed: The corrigendum's specific corrections are unknown. The draft uses figures of '50 studies', '16 of 41 countries', and the claim that 'no studies reporting on how teachers could support positive student behaviour' — none of these can be confirmed as matching the corrected version. The draft's own disclaimer ('nothing on this page draws on it') is contradicted by the body text, which does cite this source for substantive claims.
